nodes.question: How do regional temperature records in Connecticut compare to global temperature records?
nodes.answer: The regional temperature record in Connecticut tracked the global temperature increase closely, suggesting that similar comparisons could be made for other regions with long-term temperature records.
nodes.paragraph: Easy-to-read visuals of warming for the globe, regions, countries and towns are available in the ShowYourStripes website [7] 365 Environmental Chemistry Letters (2025) 23:363 366 [5]. However, significant proof of an anthropogenic effect is provided by observed historical records of atmospheric carbon dioxide levels, carbon-isotopic compositions, and temperatures. Regional temperatures As scientists, and as colleagues to some of the deep ice-core investigators who identified the rise in carbon dioxide on earth during the past century and a half, we plotted a cen - tury-scale record of Connecticut S average air temperature to compare to preceding global records of atmospheric car - bon dioxide (CO2) and air temperatures. distinct average increase of air temperatures of 1.99 degrees C from 1896 to 2023 in Connecticut. In large measure, the regional (Connecticut) temperature record tracked the global temperature increase. We submit that similar comparisons of regional temperatures to global temperatures could illustra- tively be produced for any region around the world for which long-term temperature records were available. In the absence of global warming or climate change, all of the three preceding graphs should have been flat.

nodes.question: What three key indices are increasing according to the paragraph?
nodes.answer: The three key indices that are increasing are global atmospheric pCO2, average global temperature, and average Connecticut air temperature.
nodes.paragraph: In fact, all three key indices are distinctly increasing at accelerated rates toward the upper right, i.e., into the present and the near future: the global atmospheric pCO2, the average global temperature, and the average Connecticut air temperature. Taken together, global CO2 rise is consistent with global- and regional air temperature increase. Further, NOAA National Centers for Environmental State Climate Summa- ries 2022 project that Connecticut temperatures will increase by approximately 1.4 to 7.8 degrees by year 2100. Further exhaustive evidence of human influence on the climate sys- tem is reported in the IPCC Sixth Assessment [8 ].Why be concerned? Because we are variously degrading our environment in barely-perceptible slow motion barely perceptible by human observational scales, but made clear here by scien- tific graphical presentation. Regarding a resolution of the global climatic problem, an eminent marine geochemist recently aptly stated that we will need to markedly decrease the atmospheric CO2 level and to substantially decrease the input of CO2 into the atmosphere from fossil fuel and bio - mass burning as well as to increase the CO2 removal. For that, research is actively developing solutions to sequester CO2 [9].

nodes.question: What was the temperature increase from the lowest to the highest observed in seawater temperatures from Dalian to Fujian?
nodes.answer: The lowest temperature increased by 14 degrees, while the highest temperature increased by 8 degrees.
nodes.paragraph: S. japonica immigrated > 3,400 km in distance and about 17 degree in latitude from Hokkaido (Japan) to Dalian, then Shan - dong Peninsula and Fujian coasts. From Dalian to Fujian, the summer seawater temperature increases from ~ 3 in Jan., < 1 in Feb. and ~ 17 in Jun [ 10]. to ~ 21 in Nov., 15 in Mar. and 25 in Jun. (Saojun Pang, per - sonal communication). The lowest temperature increased by 14 while the highest temperature increased by 8 . S. japonica has adapted to relative high seawater tem - perature. Brown algae may shift their habitats northward, and lose their diversity [ 11]. Unfortunately, the physical and genetic bases underlining the adaptation of kelp to relative high seawater temperature remain unclear. Genetically, the sex is a separating and mixing pro - cess of genomes, which encompasses diverse systems and mechanisms [ 12]. Except for the sex chromosomes and master sex determination gene, intrinsic and extrin - sic environments may also play roles in sex determina - tion. The model brown alga Ectocarpus determines its gender with the sex determination region on U (female) and V (male) chromosomes, respectively [ 13, 14], and the HMG-sex has been identified as the male-determiner of Ectocarpus gametophytes [ 15].

nodes.question: What role does climate change play in the dynamics of MHWs in Chesapeake Bay?
nodes.answer: Climate change plays a key role by contributing to increases in MHW frequency primarily driven by long-term warming from anthropogenic climate change.
nodes.paragraph: The lack of understanding of MHWs in estuarine systems can largely be attributed to the challenges in observing water temperature at a sufficient temporal resolution (at least daily) and maintaining the long-term records, on the order of decades, necessary to accurately characterize these events37,47,49. While satellite data are effective for broader oceanic and continental shelf studies, they often fail to accurately resolve nearshore and 1Virginia Institute of Marine Science, William & Mary, Gloucester Point, VA, USA. 2Physics Department, California Polytechnic State University, San Luis Obispo, CA, USA. email: rutzignardi@vims.edu OPEN Scientific Reports www.nature.com/scientificreports estuarine environments due to their complex shorelines and smaller spatial scales36,37,49. As a result, research using continuous, long-term in-situ data to explore the physical mechanisms behind MHWs in estuaries has been limited, despite the major ecosystem implications36,48,49. Recent research found that in Chesapeake Bay, the largest estuary in the United States, both climate change and variability played a key role in the dynamics of MHWs49. In addition to documenting increases in MHW frequency primarily driven by long-term warming resulting from anthropogenic climate change, similar to trends observed in the global ocean, they also found significant changes in the likelihood of MHW occurrence in response to different phases of climate modes of variability14,15,49.
